learnings.title: Getting dressed
learnings.focus: The daily wrestle with buttons and socks — full of fine motor practice, and the first place a toddler insists on doing it themselves.

themes.title: Buttons, zips, and getting there myself
themes.detail: Doing up a button, working a zip, pulling on socks — the fiddly motor skill getting dressed asks for every day, moving from needing help to graduated help to none at all.

themes.title: Two things, in order
themes.detail: "Vest on, then socks" — a two-part instruction the child has to hold in mind and act on in the right order, with a "why" thrown in when they ask.

themes.title: Naming what's going on
themes.detail: Colours, textures, the names of what's being pulled on and off — narrated out loud, it floods the child with rich, precise words for something they're already looking at.

themes.title: Choosing, and wanting to do it myself
themes.detail: Picking what to wear is one of a toddler's first real choices, and the "me do it" phase that comes with it is healthy — met best with calm, consistent patience rather than a rush.

themes.title: First this, then that
themes.detail: Getting dressed has a natural order — pants before trousers, socks before shoes — and putting words to it ("first... then...") is early sequencing, for real.

learnings.title: Garden & park play
learnings.focus: The part of the day that happens outdoors — running about, balls, mud and whatever's growing — and the only one that asks for the whole body at once.

themes.title: Running, wheeling, out of breath
themes.detail: Outside is where the big movements live — running, climbing, a scooter or a trike, hopping across the grass, balancing along a low wall. It's also the part of the day a child properly gets out of breath, which under-fives need daily rather than weekly.

themes.title: Balls, and getting them where you want
themes.detail: Kicking, throwing, catching — starting as a two-handed scramble at a big ball, and slowly turning into aim: passing to someone, hitting what they meant to hit, judging how hard.

themes.title: Handfuls of the natural world
themes.detail: Leaves, conkers, bark, stones, a snail on the path — picked up, turned over, smelled, carried home in a pocket. Seeds and bulbs that get planted and then checked on for weeks, and the gentleness that comes with something being alive.

themes.title: Weather, seasons and things that push back
themes.detail: Rain on the face, wind moving the trees, mud that sticks and puddles that splash. The same park looks nothing like itself in October and June — and a swing being pushed or a wagon pulled is a child's first honest encounter with a force.

themes.title: Words for what's out there
themes.detail: Outside hands over words nothing indoors does — knobbly, prickly, soggy, damp — because the child is holding the thing while the word for it arrives, and describing what they can see, hear and smell while they're standing in it.

themes.title: Mud, sticks and repeating patterns
themes.detail: Mark-making without paper — fingers through mud, a stick dragged across gravel. And what gets collected tends to get laid out in a line, stick, leaf, stick, leaf, which is the first repeating pattern a child makes for themselves.

learnings.title: Washing & teeth
learnings.focus: The short, repeated bits of the day — hands, face, teeth, the toilet — where a child slowly takes over looking after their own body.

themes.title: Doing it myself
themes.detail: Brushing teeth, washing hands, managing the toilet — the same few jobs every single day, moving from done-for-them, to done-with-help, to done alone without anyone asking.

themes.title: The toilet, at their own pace
themes.detail: Readiness shows itself — noticing a wet nappy, longer dry stretches, saying they need to go — and it goes best as friendly co-operation rather than a deadline somebody else set.

themes.title: Teeth, morning and night
themes.detail: One of the first things in a child's life that happens twice a day, every day, whether they feel like it or not — as much the shape of a habit as a clean mouth.

themes.title: Knowing why, not just when
themes.detail: Washing sticks once the reason comes with it — that hands carry things you can't see, and that looking after your own body is something you do on purpose.

themes.title: Before eating, after the toilet
themes.detail: Two fixed hinges in the day, and a child who has the words for them has somewhere to hang washing — a moment of its own rather than a random interruption.

learnings.title: Drawing & making
learnings.focus: Paper, pens and a box of junk — the quietest stretch of the day, and the one quietly building the hand that will write.

themes.title: The hand that will hold a pencil
themes.detail: Pinching a crayon between thumb and fingers, snipping with scissors, one hand steadily becoming the one that does the fiddly work — the whole apparatus handwriting needs later, built while the child thinks they're just colouring in.

themes.title: Marks that mean something
themes.detail: The point where a scribble stops being a scribble — "that says mummy", the first letter of a name, a pretend list down the side of the page, an amount recorded in whatever squiggles the child invents for it.

themes.title: Colour, and what things feel like
themes.detail: Paint on fingers, clay, fabric, cornflour and mud — colours getting named while they're being used, and materials sorted by hand into the rough and the smooth, the sticky and the dry.

themes.title: Having an idea, then making it
themes.detail: Rummaging through the box before settling on what it's going to be, a circle that turns into a face, a cereal box that is definitely a rocket — the thing carries an idea the child had first.

themes.title: Shapes that stack and fit
themes.detail: Blocks, inset puzzles, the flat-sided piece that goes on the bottom and the pointy one that makes the roof — shape learned by whether it works, long before it's learned by name.

themes.title: Talk while the hands are busy
themes.detail: One of the calmest talking stretches in the day — hands occupied, heads side by side — and the words that come with it, up and down and round and back, land attached to something actually being done.

learnings.title: Bedtime
learnings.focus: The quietest stretch of the day, and the one that carries more books, rhymes and settling than any other.

themes.title: The story before lights out
themes.detail: A book at the end of the day, the same favourites asked for again and again, joining in with the lines they know by heart — and afterwards, who in it was brave and who was kind.

themes.title: Words that only live in books
themes.detail: Stories carry words the day never says out loud — enormous, invitation, caterpillar — and the back-and-forth about what's happening on the page is where a child picks them up.

themes.title: How a book works
themes.detail: Which way up it goes, the cover and whose name is on it, words running along the line, pages turning in order — all soaked up from being the one holding it.

themes.title: Rhymes and songs at the end of the day
themes.detail: The wind-down songs and the rhymes that always come next — the rhythm of them, the beats inside words, and the last word of a line filled in before it arrives.

themes.title: The same order, every night
themes.detail: Bath, pyjamas, teeth, two stories, lights out — an order a child comes to know well enough to say what's coming next, and the before / then / after that words that ride along with it.

themes.title: Settling down
themes.detail: Winding down with someone calm close by, the blanket or bear that has to be within reach, and sleep quietly taking its place among the things a child knows keep them well.

learnings.title: Bath & water play
learnings.focus: A tub, a couple of cups and something to pour with — the everyday place a child first works out bigger, smaller and which one holds more.

themes.title: Bigger, smaller, heavier
themes.detail: Showing with hands and saying it in words — "bigger", "smaller", "tall", "heavy" — comparing one thing in the water against another, the first informal measuring talk.

themes.title: Which cup holds more
themes.detail: Two containers side by side, and a question that gets answered by pouring rather than counting — the everyday version of capacity, worked out with cups, jugs and whatever's floating in the tub.

themes.title: Longer, heavier, more of it
themes.detail: A sponge, a duck, a toy boat — sized up directly against another rather than against a memory of what came before, weighed in the hand or laid end to end.

themes.title: A guess, then the pour that checks it
themes.detail: Which one turns out to hold more — guessed first, then tested by pouring — and the word that reports the result: this one holds more than that one.
